1.title: Data Ingestion and Transformation
1.text: Welcome to Module ten: Data Ingestion and Transformation. This module covers task statement three point five, the last task of Domain three. You will choose ingestion patterns, design streaming pipelines, transform and convert data, build and secure a data lake, and query it. The exam describes data arriving at some speed, and asks you to pick the services from ingestion to dashboard.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Choose an ingestion pattern by frequency, size and speed. Design streaming pipelines with Kinesis, Firehose, Flink and M S K. Transform data and convert formats with Glue. Build and secure a data lake with S three, Glue and Lake Formation. And query and visualize with Athena, OpenSearch and Quick, and transfer data with DataSync.

1.title: Case Check-In: Lantern and Loom Learns from Its Data
1.text: Lantern and Loom wants to learn from its data. Clickstream events pour in all day. Order exports arrive each night as C S V, short for comma-separated values, files. C R M data sits in a software-as-a-service application, and warehouse files sit on an on-premises N A S. Analysts want S Q L on S three and dashboards, with customer columns restricted. Your job is to choose the ingestion, transformation, security and analytics services.

1.title: Data Ingestion Patterns
1.text: Start with the pattern. Streaming means events arrive continuously and results are needed in seconds; use Kinesis Data Streams, M S K or Firehose. Near real time means delivering to a store within minutes; use Data Firehose. Batch means files on a schedule, hourly or nightly; use S three uploads, Glue jobs or DataSync. And software-as-a-service and partner data use AppFlow and Data Exchange. Size for volume, record size, frequency and the number of consumers. And secure each access point with I A M, V P C endpoints and encryption. Exam tip: seconds mean streaming, hours mean batch, and a managed pipeline into a store means Firehose.

1.title: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
1.text: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams collects and processes large streams of records in real time. A record is usually readable in under a second. A stream is made of shards, and each shard takes about one megabyte or one thousand records per second in, and two megabytes per second out. On-demand mode scales automatically, while provisioned mode needs a shard count you set. Several consumers can read the same stream independently, and enhanced fan-out gives each its own throughput. Order is kept per shard, chosen by the partition key, so pick a well-spread key. Exam tip: many consumers, replayable and real-time points to Kinesis Data Streams; unknown traffic points to on-demand mode.

1.title: Amazon Data Firehose and Managed Service for Apache Flink
1.text: Two services process streams in different ways. Amazon Data Firehose, formerly Kinesis Data Firehose, is a fully managed delivery service. It buffers by size or time, can transform records with Lambda, and can convert them to Parquet or O R C. Use it to load streams into S three, Redshift, OpenSearch, Splunk, Iceberg tables or H T T P endpoints, with no code. Managed Service for Apache Flink, formerly Kinesis Data Analytics, runs Apache Flink in Java, Scala, Python or S Q L. Use it for real-time analytics, windowing and streaming E T L. Exam tip: to load a stream into S three with no servers, use Firehose; to compute on the stream, use Managed Flink.

1.title: A Streaming Architecture
1.text: Here is a streaming architecture. Producers write to Kinesis Data Streams. A Flink application computes live metrics from the stream. Firehose delivers the raw events to S three as Parquet. Athena queries the lake, and Quick shows dashboards. The figure shows producers feeding a stream that branches to live Flink metrics and Firehose delivery into an S three lake. Exam tip: one stream can feed real-time processing and durable storage in parallel.

1.title: Amazon MSK and Kinesis Video Streams
1.text: Amazon M S K is managed Apache Kafka, as provisioned clusters or M S K Serverless, and M S K Connect moves data in and out. Choose it when you already use Kafka and want open-source compatibility. Kinesis Data Streams is the A W S-native option with shards, for A W S integration and simple operations. Kinesis Video Streams streams live video and time-serialized data from devices, for analytics and playback; use it for cameras and sensors. M S K runs brokers in each zone and replaces failed brokers automatically. Exam tip: existing Kafka applications mean M S K; video from devices means Kinesis Video Streams.

1.title: AWS Glue: Catalog, Crawlers and ETL
1.text: A W S Glue is serverless data integration. The Data Catalog is a central metadata store that Athena, E M R and Redshift Spectrum read. Crawlers infer schemas and fill the catalog automatically. E T L jobs run on Apache Spark, built visually in Glue Studio or in code, on a schedule, on demand, or on an event. DataBrew cleans data without code. A typical transform is C S V to Parquet. Exam tip: cataloging, crawling and transforming without servers is Glue, and converting C S V to Parquet is a Glue job.

1.title: Building a Data Lake
1.text: A data lake keeps raw and curated data in S three. The Glue Data Catalog describes it. Lake Formation adds central permissions over the catalog and the data. Athena, E M R, Redshift Spectrum and Quick all read the same lake. Partition by date, and use columnar formats for speed and cost. The figure shows sources feeding raw and curated zones in S three, with the catalog and Lake Formation above, and query engines beside. Exam tip: many tools and one lake means S three data, a Glue catalog and Lake Formation permissions.

1.title: Securing a Data Lake with Lake Formation
1.text: Lake Formation centrally governs, secures and shares data lake data on S three and its Glue Data Catalog metadata. Its permissions add to I A M, with grant and revoke like a database. You control access at the database, table, column, row and cell level, and Athena, Redshift Spectrum, E M R, Glue and Quick respect it. L F tags manage thousands of permissions with a few tags. It supports cross-account sharing, and hybrid access mode lets you adopt it step by step. CloudTrail audits access, you encrypt S three with K M S, and you secure ingestion endpoints with I A M, T L S and V P C endpoints. Exam tip: column or row restrictions on a data lake mean Lake Formation permissions.

2.title: Querying and Visualizing Data
2.text: Four services query and show data. Amazon Athena is serverless S Q L directly on S three, with no infrastructure, for ad hoc queries on the lake. Amazon OpenSearch Service is a managed search and analytics engine with dashboards, for log analytics, search and real-time monitoring. Amazon E M R runs managed Spark and Hadoop, for heavy transformations and large analytics. And Amazon Quick, formerly QuickSight, builds dashboards for business users. To cut Athena cost and time, use Parquet or O R C, partitions, compression and sensible file sizes. Exam tip: S Q L on S three with no servers is Athena; charts for managers is Quick.

2.title: Data Transfer and Integration Services
2.text: Several services move data in. A W S DataSync transfers online from N F S, S M B, H D F S or object storage to S three, E F S or F S x, on a schedule, encrypted and integrity-checked. Storage Gateway gives hybrid access to cloud storage from on premises; module six covered it. Amazon AppFlow runs no-code flows between software-as-a-service applications and A W S, on demand, on a schedule or on an event. A W S Data Exchange finds and subscribes to third-party data sets. The Snow Family and Transfer Family handle offline and file-protocol transfers; module eleven covers them. As of the fifth of November, twenty twenty-six, A W S Data Pipeline is in maintenance mode and closed to new customers, so use Glue or Step Functions. Exam tip: on-premises files to S three over the network is DataSync; software-as-a-service to A W S with no code is AppFlow.

2.title: Choosing Ingestion and Analytics Services
2.text: Here is the chooser. Real-time with many consumers and replay is Kinesis Data Streams. Loading a stream into S three or Redshift with no code is Data Firehose. Computing on a stream is Managed Flink. Kafka applications use M S K. Cataloging and transforming is Glue. S Q L on S three is Athena. Column and row security is Lake Formation. Dashboards are Quick. And bulk files from on premises use DataSync. Exam tip: name the stage: ingest, transform, secure, query or show.

2.title: What the Exam Asks: Ingestion and Transformation
2.text: Here is what the exam asks. Which ingestion service for the speed, size and consumers. Which transformation: Glue, Firehose, Flink or E M R. Which format and layout: Parquet, partitions or compression. Which security control: Lake Formation, I A M, V P C endpoints or K M S. And which transfer service: DataSync, AppFlow, Snow or Data Exchange. Exam tip: underline seconds, hours, S Q L, Kafka, software-as-a-service and restricted columns.

2.title: Design Check: Lantern and Loom Learns from Its Data
2.text: Here is the Design Check. Cover the right column and answer each row yourself. Clickstream with several teams and replay: Kinesis Data Streams. Raw events to S three as Parquet with no consumer code: Data Firehose with format conversion. Nightly C S V exports made fast to query: a Glue job to Parquet, partitioned by date. Analysts want S Q L on S three: Amazon Athena over the Glue Data Catalog. Customer columns restricted: Lake Formation column-level permissions. C R M data into the lake: Amazon AppFlow. Warehouse N A S files to S three: A W S DataSync. And dashboards: Amazon Quick.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. To ingest, use Kinesis Data Streams, Firehose, M S K and Flink, and batch with S three, Glue and DataSync. To transform, use Glue for C S V to Parquet, and E M R for heavy jobs. The lake is S three plus the Glue Data Catalog plus Lake Formation. To query and show, use Athena, OpenSearch and Quick. And to move data, use DataSync, AppFlow and Data Exchange.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. Lantern and Loom's site produces thousands of clickstream events per second. Several teams must read the same events independently in real time, and one team may need to re-read the last few hours. Which service fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. It supports multiple independent consumers, and lets them read recent data again. A queue gives each message to one consumer.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Clickstream events must land in Amazon S three as Parquet files within minutes, and the team does not want to write or run any consumer code. Which solution fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Amazon Data Firehose with record format conversion turned on. It buffers records, converts them to Parquet, and writes them to S three without code.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. Analysts query large C S V files in Amazon S three with Athena, and the queries are slow and costly. Which change helps most? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: convert the data to Parquet and partition it by date. Columnar formats and partitions let Athena read less data. One large gzip file cannot be split for parallel reads.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. Select two. Which two statements about A W S Lake Formation are correct? The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and C. Lake Formation can restrict access at the column, row and cell level, and L F tags let a few tags control access to many resources. Data stays in S three and should still be encrypted, and Lake Formation supports cross-account sharing.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Lantern and Loom must copy forty terabytes of warehouse files from an on-premises N F S server to Amazon S three over the network, on a schedule, with encryption and integrity checks. Which service should it use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A W S DataSync. It automates online transfers from N F S and S M B sources to S three, with scheduling, encryption and data integrity validation.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all five answers. Question one: C. Question two: A. Question three: D. Question four: A and C. Question five: B. That completes the three content domains so far. In Module eleven, we begin Domain four: cost-optimized storage.
